authenticity.evidence: GeckoTerminal shows 2,064 unique buyers but only 55 unique sellers in the first hour. The seller count was stuck at 48 across the m5, m15 and m30 windows, yet those 48 wallets made 2,855 sells in 30 minutes. That pattern points to a small set of market-maker or wash bots cycling volume. $5.2M of volume on a ~$115k market cap is 32x turnover in one hour. GMGN flags 48 bundler wallets, with a top-bundler trader share of 23%. There are no smart or renowned wallets and no degen calls. The project X account (wenpcfamily) has launched 48 tokens. The pool was created directly on PumpSwap with unlocked LP, and RugCheck reports few LP providers.
authenticity.uncertainty: The buyer count could include real retail who followed the NPCs meta from the $9.4M pump.fun original. GMGN reports bot_degen_rate as 0, which conflicts with the seller pattern. I can't see any X posts.

structured_output.counterargument: NPCs is clearly a live meta today: one pump.fun version reached a $9.4M market cap about 3 hours ago, and several copies hit $1-4M. This token still has $160k of liquidity and more than 2,000 buyers, and it is at its all-time high with no sign of a sell-off yet. If the wenpc.family team treats this as their flagship and leaves the LP in, a meta rotation could carry it from $115k to $230k+ fast. That only takes one more leg on a coin that already rose 135% in an hour.

structural_risks: The LP is 0% locked or burned, and the pool was seeded directly on PumpSwap, so the deployer or LP provider can pull liquidity at any time
RugCheck flags 'Low amount of LP Providers'
At least 7 same-name 'NPCs' copies created in the last ~5 hours now show $0 liquidity, including non-pump-address deploys like this one, which fits a repeated pull-LP pattern
The project X account has launched 48 tokens, which looks like a serial deployer
About 55 seller wallets generate thousands of sells, so the volume looks artificial and depth is overstated

narrative.description: This is an 'NPCs' copycat riding a same-day NPC meta. It was deployed through wenpc.family, a site that seems to launch many NPC-branded tokens. It also reuses the ticker of the established Non-Playable Coin ($NPC).
narrative.why_spreading: A pump.fun 'NPCs' token ran to about $9.4M today. That set off a wave of same-name copies, and this one is catching the spillover, helped by heavy bot-driven volume.

source_coverage.notes: No internet access in this condition. This report uses only the evidence packet.

structured_output.thesis: This is a late, non-canonical 'NPCs' clone from a serial deployer site (wenpc.family, whose X account has launched 48 tokens). It sits in an unlocked, deployer-seeded PumpSwap pool. The volume looks wash-traded: about 55 sellers against 2,000+ buyers. Several sibling NPCs deploys from the last few hours already show $0 liquidity. The most likely outcome is an LP pull or collapse, not a further 2x from a 25-minute-delayed entry.

token_connection.why_this_token: It shares the NPCs name and ticker with the meta leader, and it was created on wenpc.family.
token_connection.competing_tokens: The meta leader is the pump.fun 'NPCs' token 68SV...pump, at a $9.4M market cap with $273k liquidity. At least 7 other 'NPCs' clones now show $0 liquidity. The established Non-Playable Coin (NPC) has $86M and $189M listings. RugCheck labels this token a 'Copycat token'.

unknowns: Who provided the LP and whether they intend to pull it

structured_output.what_is_happening: NPC (NPCs) is a 37-minute-old PumpSwap pair at about a $115k market cap. It is up 135% in an hour on $5.2M of volume. It was not launched on the pump.fun curve: the pool was seeded directly, and 0% of the LP is locked. It is one of many 'NPCs' clones riding a same-day meta whose pump.fun leader reached $9.4M, and most of the other clones already show zero liquidity.
